title: Epoxide opening in base
subtitle: Methoxide attacks the less hindered carbon of an epoxide

reactants.caption: 2,2-dimethyloxirane + sodium methoxide, in methanol
reactants.learnerPrompt: Methoxide opens the epoxide. Which carbon does it attack?
hintTiers: Methoxide is a strong nucleophile and the ring strain makes the epoxide reactive even without acid. With no positive charge to guide it, what controls the attack in an SN2 reaction?
Methoxide attacks the less hindered CH₂ carbon, and the C–O bond to that carbon breaks onto the epoxide oxygen. Two arrows.
Methoxide lone pair → new bond to the CH₂ of the epoxide; that C–O bond → a lone pair on the epoxide oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That is the acid-catalysed regiochemistry. Methoxide reacts by a plain SN2 reaction, and an SN2 reaction at a tertiary carbon is far too hindered. It attacks the CH₂.
Methanol is not acidic enough to protonate an epoxide, and with methoxide present there is no acid. The strong nucleophile opens the neutral epoxide.

alkoxide.caption: tertiary alkoxide + methanol
hintTiers: The ring opening leaves a negatively charged oxygen. Which molecule, present in large excess, can give it a proton?
The alkoxide takes the drawn proton from methanol, and the O–H pair stays on the methanol oxygen. Two arrows.
Alkoxide lone pair → new bond to the H of methanol; that O–H bond → a lone pair on the methanol oxygen (methoxide is regenerated).

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Methanol has no leaving group on its carbon. The alkoxide is a base: it takes the O–H proton.

steps.explanationAfterStep: An SN2 reaction at the less hindered carbon. The leaving group is an alkoxide, normally a poor leaving group, but the release of the ring strain (about 110 kJ mol⁻¹) pays for it.
The solvent protonates the alkoxide and gives back methoxide, so methoxide is regenerated.

mechanismSummary: Methoxide opens the strained epoxide by an SN2 reaction at the less hindered CH₂ carbon, with inversion there (invisible at a CH₂). The alkoxide formed takes a proton from methanol: 1-methoxy-2-methylpropan-2-ol. Compare acid conditions, where methanol attacks the more substituted carbon of the protonated epoxide.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 15
